budget_items.topic: Cost of posting legal ad (Sentinel vs. the Ledger)
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed whether to post the special town meeting warrant's legal ad in the daily Sentinel instead of the weekly Ledger to save time, and someone suggested the cost difference was probably minor. The board decided to stick with the Ledger for consistency with what residents expect to read.

budget_items.topic: Teamsters Union Local 170 (DPW) collective bargaining agreement
budget_items.what_was_said: The board ratified the DPW collective bargaining agreement with Teamsters Local 170, noting the board had already voted on it in executive session and was waiting on paperwork that has now been received.

public_comment.topic: His availability for a proposed special town meeting date (available Sept. 2, not Sept. 3) and the charter/statutory process for a deputy or temporary moderator to stand in if he is absent.

votes.motion: Call a special town meeting for Thursday, September 3, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. at the Lunenburg Middle High School Auditorium, per the citizens' petition, and open the warrant July 28, 2026 with it closing 5:00 p.m. Friday, August 7, 2026.
Approve the September 1, 2026 state primary election warrant.
Ratify the collective bargaining agreement with Teamsters Union Local 170 (DPW).

decisions.decision: The board will continue posting the special town meeting legal ad in the Ledger rather than switching to the daily Sentinel, for consistency.
The board agreed to try to confirm deputy moderator Rob Bowen's availability for September 3rd before/while proceeding, though the meeting date was set regardless.
The pre-town-meeting moderator's meeting (normally run by the moderator) will be open to anyone who might serve as the temporary moderator on September 3rd.

minutes.summary: The Select Board set the schedule for a citizen-petition special town meeting for September 3, 2026, working through a tight statutory timeline for the warrant, legal ad, FinCom public hearing and mailed notices, complicated by town moderator Tim Murphy's unavailability that date. The board also approved the September 1 state primary election warrant and ratified the DPW collective bargaining agreement with Teamsters Local 170, then adjourned to meet again the next evening in a joint workshop with the Municipal Building Design Committee.
minutes.headline: The Select Board called a citizen-petition special town meeting for September 3, setting the warrant and hearing schedule.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to call a citizen-petition special town meeting for September 3, 2026, opening the warrant July 28 and closing it August 7.
The board is still working to line up a stand-in moderator for that night, since town moderator Tim Murphy told the board he is unavailable September 3.
The board approved the warrant for the September 1 state primary election.
The board ratified the DPW collective bargaining agreement with Teamsters Local 170, following an earlier executive-session vote.
The board chose to keep running the special town meeting's legal ad in the weekly Ledger rather than switch to the daily Sentinel.

why_it_matters: The September 3 special town meeting is where residents act on the citizen petition's warrant article, and the schedule set here fixes the deadlines for that vote.
Who presides as moderator affects how that meeting is run, and the board is still confirming a deputy or temporary moderator can serve.
The ratified DPW union contract sets pay and working terms that flow into future town budgets.
watch_next: The September 3, 2026 special town meeting and its outcome on the citizen-petition warrant article
Confirmation of a temporary or deputy moderator (Rob Bowen) able to serve that night
